newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to release 100,000 tonnes sugar to ease Spanish shortage.
newsitem.headline: EU to release 100,000 tonnes sugar to ease Spanish shortage.

text.p: The European Commission will release 100,000 tonnes of sugar for Spain to ease shortages caused by floods in the south of the country, Commission officials said on Friday.
They said the Commission will press ahead even though the EU sugar management committee on Wednesday gave no opinion on the proposed move.
The Commission will allow the release this month of 29,000 tonnes of Spanish sugar held as part of the EU's minimum stocks of 400,000 tonnes.

A further 71,000 tonnes of non-quota C sugar being carried forward into 1997/98 (July/June), which is normally blocked until December, will be released in July as quota sugar, a Commission sugar official said.
The Commission is taking this emergency measure under article 27 of the basic EU sugar regulation 1785/81.
Several member states, which were unhappy about this solution, voted against but were unable to achieve enough votes to reject it. Neither were there sufficient votes in favour.
Under EU rules, the Commission can now take the initiative and implement the proposal.
The sugar committee is expected next week to approve a most-favoured-nation (MFN) raw cane sugar import quota of 85,463 tonnes for 1997/98 (July/June), the officials added.
The sugar would be supplied by Cuba, Brazil and other countries at a reduced tariff of 98 ecus a tonne.

The annual quota, which corresponds to 82,000 tonnes of white sugar equivalent, mainly compensates Finland's traditional suppliers under the former General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) for trade losses after it joined the EU.
The sugar panel is also expected next week to approve 1997/98 (July/June) subsidised sugar supplies for remote islands.

On Wednesday, the European Commission proposed that supplies to the Portuguese Azores should be increased by 1,000 tonnes to 6,500 tonnes due to expectations of a poor crop for the second successive year.
Supplies for the Spanish Canary Islands and Portuguese Madeira would remain virtually unchanged at 60,000 tonnes and 10,000 tonnes respectively.

Supplies for a group of more accessible Greek Aegean islands would be reduced to 600 tonnes, from 3,000 tonnes in 1996/97, but deliveries to the more remote islands would be little changed at 9,000 tonnes.
EU molasses import duties will remain suspended for another week until June 19.
The cif reference price for cane molasses was set at 8.29 Ecus per 100 kg, compared with 8.38 Ecus the previous week.
The cif price for beet molasses was set at 12.12 Ecus per 100 kg, against 12.23 Ecus last week.
